session_tail:
Aborting the distillation. The novelty self-gate does not pass.

The only generalizable lesson from this session is "don't `json.dumps()` text you are about to run a word tokenizer over, because the escape welds a stray `n` onto the next token." A fresh Claude already knows JSON escaping alters text. This was a failure of attention, not of knowledge, so saving it would put junk in an empty library. It is also a single fact rather than a procedure, and I cannot write a verification command that fails when the lesson is skipped, which rule 8 requires. The library has no existing skill to update either.

The test work is done. All 22 tests in the detection suite pass, and the full suite is green at 135 passed.

Two bugs in `scripts/detect.py`, both real root causes rather than test-shaped patches:

- **Response flattening destroyed token boundaries.** `response_text` serialized non-string tool responses with `json.dumps`, turning a real newline into a literal backslash-n. The tokenizer then produced `nwidgetflushederror` instead of two tokens, so any symptom that begins a line stopped matching. It now walks the structure and joins the string leaves with newlines, which fixes the nested-dict case for free.
- **The symptom injection path never recorded fingerprint attribution.** The prompt path in `scripts/retrieve.py` computed `preexisting_fingerprint`; the detection path logged `None` unconditionally. It now reuses `retrieve.fingerprint_preexisting` under the same probe cap, so both injection paths report the same field.

```
python3 -m pytest tests/ -q
135 passed in 1.51s
```

Skipped: no shared helper extracted for the two injection paths. They differ in budget and trigger, and one duplicated four-line block is cheaper than the wrong abstraction. Add one when a third injection path appears.
